title: Descent of the full tensor bifunctor shift structure and normalized fixed comparisons
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site and $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, with module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], unbounded derived category $D(R)$ and homotopy localization $Q_h:K(R)\to D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], which commutes with shifts [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated]. Let $\mathcal P_R\subset K(R)$ be the flat-term K-flat complexes [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, def-pc-kflat-complex], and assume $\mathcal P_R$ is stable under every integer shift. Use the published total-tensor-derived bifunctor $T$ and its natural representative isomorphisms $c_{P,S}:Q_h\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_R S)\cong T(Q_hP,Q_hS)$, resolving localization equivalence and arbitrary-transformation extension property [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Total tensor means [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves].
There exist unique natural isomorphisms $t^1_n:T(M[n],N)\cong T(M,N)[n]$ and $t^2_n:T(M,N[n])\cong T(M,N)[n]$ for all integers $n$ and $M,N\in D(R)$, whose restrictions along $Q_h|_{\mathcal P_R}\times Q_h|_{\mathcal P_R}$ are $Q_hs^1_n,Q_hs^2_n$ of [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-integer-shifts], conjugated by $c$ and the canonical shift comparisons of $Q_h$. They satisfy the zero-shift and addition-of-shifts identities. For every pair of integers $a,b$, the two maps $T(M[a],N[b])\to T(M,N)[a+b]$ obtained by extracting shifts in the two orders differ by $(-1)^{ab}$ under the canonical identification of iterated shifts. Thus $t^1,t^2$ give one coherent integer bifunctor shift structure on this specified $T$.
For every derived morphism $f:M\to M'$, the transformation $T(f,-)$ commutes with $t^2_n$; for every derived morphism $g:N\to N'$, $T(-,g)$ commutes with $t^1_n$. These include chain maps between resolving complexes, inverses of their quasi-isomorphisms, and arbitrary words in their localization, independently of the chosen word.
Fix $A\in\mathcal P_R$ and put $H_A(B)=\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes_R B)$ and $H^A(B)=\operatorname{Tot}(B\otimes_R A)$, assumed to induce functors on $K(R)$ preserving quasi-isomorphisms and equipped with $s^2_n,s^1_n$. Any natural isomorphisms $e_{L,B}:Q_hH_A(B)\cong T(Q_hA,Q_hB)$ and $e_{R,B}:Q_hH^A(B)\cong T(Q_hB,Q_hA)$ whose components on $B\in\mathcal P_R$ are exactly $c_{A,B},c_{B,A}$ commute with the signed shifts for every $B\in K(R)$. Consequently the restrictions of $t^2,t^1$ at $Q_hA$ agree, under these comparisons, with the one-variable shifts descended from $H_A,H^A$. No boundedness is imposed.

proof.text:
Put $L=Q_h|_{\mathcal P_R}$ and write $\lambda_n(X):Q_h(X[n])\cong Q_h(X)[n]$ for the coherent comparisons of [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated]. The total tensor of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] has the natural chain comparisons $s^i_n$ of [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-integer-shifts]; their naturality passes to homotopy classes by applying the quotient functor. Shift stability ensures $P[n],S[n]\in\mathcal P_R$. Define a natural isomorphism on resolving pairs by the following composite, written in order of application:
$$T(LP[n],LS)\xrightarrow{T(\lambda_n(P)^{-1},1)}T(L(P[n]),LS)\xrightarrow{c_{P[n],S}^{-1}}Q_h\operatorname{Tot}(P[n]\otimes S)\xrightarrow{Q_hs^1_n}Q_h(\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes S)[n])\xrightarrow{\lambda_n(\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes S))}Q_h\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes S)[n]\xrightarrow{c_{P,S}[n]}T(LP,LS)[n].$$
Call it $\delta^1_n(P,S)$. Define $\delta^2_n$ by replacing the first arrow with $T(1,\lambda_n(S)^{-1})$, the next comparison with $c_{P,S[n]}^{-1}$, and the middle chain map with $Q_hs^2_n$. Naturality of $c$ in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], of $\lambda$, and of the chain comparisons proves naturality of these composites in both homotopy-category variables. Every arrow used here is an isomorphism.

For $i=1,2$, let $U^1_n(M,N)=T(M[n],N)$, $U^2_n(M,N)=T(M,N[n])$, and $V_n(M,N)=T(M,N)[n]$. The arbitrary-transformation extension clause of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], with target $D(R)$, extends $\delta^i_n$ uniquely to $t^i_n:U^i_n\to V_n$. Apply the same clause to $(\delta^i_n)^{-1}$ to obtain $u^i_n:V_n\to U^i_n$. Both $u^i_nt^i_n$ and the identity restrict to the identity on resolving pairs, and likewise for $t^i_nu^i_n$. The uniqueness clause makes these composites identities. Hence $t^i_n$ is a natural isomorphism. Any other natural isomorphism with the prescribed restriction has the same underlying transformation, again by uniqueness. This constructs the structures on the specified published $T$, without replacing that bifunctor.

source.place: Tag 04VK (lemma-properties-right-localization), arbitrary-transformation enhancement in the cited descent node

proof.text: For the zero law, compare $t^i_0$ with the canonical zero-shift identification. For the addition law, compare $t^i_{a+b}$ with the composite extracting $b$ and then $a$, inserting the canonical source and target shift-addition isomorphisms. In each case the two sides are natural transformations between the same bifunctors on $D(R)\times D(R)$. Restrict along $L\times L$. A component evaluated at a shifted object such as $(LP)[a]$, which is not itself of the form $L(P')$, is first rewritten by naturality of $t^i_b$ in that variable along the isomorphism $\lambda_a(P):L(P[a])\to(LP)[a]$; since $P[a]\in\mathcal P_R$, this replaces it by $\delta^i_b(P[a],S)$ of Step 1, conjugated by $\lambda_a(P)$. Substitute the composites in Step 1: consecutive $c^{-1}c$ cancel, and naturality moves the remaining $c$ past the canonical shift isomorphisms. The zero and addition laws for $\lambda$ hold by [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated]. The resulting equality is precisely the corresponding zero or addition law for $Q_hs^i$, supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-integer-shifts]. Faithfulness of restriction in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] gives the desired equality on all derived pairs. All shifted representatives used in this restriction remain in $\mathcal P_R$ by hypothesis.

For fixed $a,b$, form the two composites from $T(M[a],N[b])$ to $T(M,N)[a+b]$, one extracting the first shift first and the other extracting the second shift first. They are natural transformations in $(M,N)$. On resolving pairs, substitute Step 1 and cancel the intermediate representative comparisons as in Step 3. Coherence of $\lambda$ identifies the two target iterated shifts. The remaining equality, including its sign, is the mixed-shift identity of [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-integer-shifts]. Concretely, on a summand whose first-factor degree in $P[a]$ is $p$, extracting the second shift first contributes $(-1)^{bp}$, whereas extracting the first shift first leaves first degree $p+a$ and contributes $(-1)^{b(p+a)}$; their quotient is $(-1)^{ab}$. The additive localization $Q_h$ preserves this sign, and conjugating by $c$ preserves multiplication by $-1$ in the additive derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Thus the two transformations, with the sign inserted, have equal restrictions. Faithfulness in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] makes them equal globally. Together with Step 3 this is the claimed coherent integer bifunctor shift structure.

Naturality of the transformation $t^2_n$ constructed in Step 2, evaluated at $(f,1_N)$, is exactly
$$t^2_n(M',N)\circ T(f,1_{N[n]})=T(f,1_N)[n]\circ t^2_n(M,N).$$
Naturality of $t^1_n$ at $(1_M,g)$ gives the other required square. Here $f,g$ are arbitrary morphisms in $D(R)$; there is no restriction to chain maps. In particular a square for an invertible $f$ implies the square for $f^{-1}$ by multiplying by the inverse vertical arrows. Squares paste under composition. Therefore they hold for inverses of quasi-isomorphisms and every localization word. If two words represent the same morphism, functoriality of $T$ makes their vertical arrows equal, proving independence of the word.

source.place: Tag 04VK (lemma-properties-right-localization); direct naturality equations for the transformations of Step 2

proof.text:
Fix $A\in\mathcal P_R$ and a normalized comparison $e_L$ as in the statement. Write $H=H_A$ and $F=T(Q_hA,-)$. For each $n$ define two transformations from $B\mapsto Q_hH(B[n])$ to $B\mapsto F(Q_hB)[n]$:
$$\alpha_B=t^2_n(Q_hA,Q_hB)\circ F(\lambda_n(B))\circ e_{L,B[n]},\qquad
\beta_B=e_{L,B}[n]\circ\lambda_n(H(B))\circ Q_h(s^2_n(A,B)).$$
Both are natural for homotopy-category maps: for $\alpha$ use naturality of $t^2_n,e_L,\lambda$, and for $\beta$ use naturality of $e_L,\lambda,s^2_n$ from [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-integer-shifts]. If $B=P\in\mathcal P_R$, then also $P[n]\in\mathcal P_R$ and normalization gives $e_{L,P}=c_{A,P}$ and $e_{L,P[n]}=c_{A,P[n]}$. Substituting Step 1 into $\alpha_P$ cancels $F(\lambda_n(P)^{-1})F(\lambda_n(P))$ and $c_{A,P[n]}^{-1}c_{A,P[n]}$, giving exactly $\beta_P$. This explicitly verifies the shift square on resolving objects.

source.place: Tag 0FNH (item-shift-tensor); sites-cohomology.tex Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor); substitution into Step 1

proof.text:
For an arbitrary $B\in K(R)$, choose a complex representing it. By [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] there is a quasi-isomorphism $r:P\to B$ with $P\in\mathcal P_R$. The shifted map $r[n]$ is a quasi-isomorphism because its cohomology maps are those of $r$ with degrees reindexed. The assumed quasi-isomorphism preservation by $H$ and the localization property [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] make $v=Q_hH(r[n])$ invertible. Naturality of the two transformations in Step 6 gives
$$\alpha_B\circ v=F(Q_hr)[n]\circ\alpha_P=F(Q_hr)[n]\circ\beta_P=\beta_B\circ v.$$
Cancel $v$ to obtain $\alpha_B=\beta_B$. This proves that every such $e_L$ commutes with shifts on all $B$. For $e_R$ repeat these same equations with $H^A$, $F=T(-,Q_hA)$, $t^1_n$, and $s^1_n(B,A)$; the normalized resolving components are $c_{P,A}$. The resolution still replaces the varying argument $B$, so the proof requires no resolution or flatness condition on its cohomology.

source.place: Tag 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution); Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor and preceding localization construction)

proof.text: Finally $Q_hH_A$ and $Q_hH^A$ invert quasi-isomorphisms by hypothesis. The localization universal property [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] descends each functor and its signed shift comparisons in one variable. More explicitly, $e_L$ exhibits $F=T(Q_hA,-)$ as a factorization of $Q_hH_A$ through $Q_h$. Conjugate $Q_hs^2_n$ using $e_L$ and $\lambda_n$; the transformation-extension clause for $Q_h$ extends this to a unique transformation $F(-[n])\to F(-)[n]$. Extend its inverse too; uniqueness makes the composites identities. The same uniqueness applied to zero and addition identities gives the one-variable coherent shifts. Steps 6-7 say exactly that $t^2_n(Q_hA,-)$ has this required conjugated restriction, so it equals that one-variable descended shift. Apply the identical argument with $e_R,H^A,s^1_n$ for $t^1_n(-,Q_hA)$. Any other factorization is identified with this one by the unique compatible natural isomorphism in the same universal property. All arguments used unbounded resolutions and direct-sum total tensor, with no boundedness assumption.
